topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: Prioritizing high-revenue services affects link budgets due to increased noise and signal degradation. The array factor plays a crucial role in managing inter-frequency band interference, with larger array sizes or closer element spacing required to mitigate interference. Non-linear amplifiers further degrade the link budget by introducing additional distortion and noise. Cognitive radio can be used to dynamically allocate frequency bands based on real-time traffic demands, optimizing link budgets while minimizing interference with navigation signals.
reference_context: Link budgets are affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling due to changes in available capacity and latency values. The main focus is to provide QoS guarantees by managing the available capacity.
